text: three_step() estimates mean external variable profile, data data frame outcome variable. default method, BCH, corrects classification error (Bolck et al., 2004; Bakk & Vermunt, 2016); standard errors clustered groups. Previous grades average 0.23 standard deviations mean enrolments first profile 0.33 enrolments second. contrast = "pairs" returns difference profile means Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value (Benjamini & Hochberg, 1995). difference -0.57 standard deviations (95% interval -0.67 -0.47). Maximum likelihood correction. method = "ml", assigned profile becomes indicator true profile whose classification errors fixed measurement model, external variable normal within profile, variance. table adds variance. variable close normal within profiles, ML usually efficient BCH (Vermunt, 2010), although classification accurate standard errors nearly equal; skewed, BCH robust choice. ML gives nearly means (0.23 -0.34), variances 0.93 0.91 within profiles. method = "modal" shows effect ignoring classification error: treats case’s probable profile known. modal means (0.22 -0.32) slightly closer together corrected ones, attenuation classification error produces; classification accurate , difference small.

text: Random effects. random = "intercept" lets students differ level ; random = "wave" level rate change. formula ~ 0 + wave gives random slope without random intercept. random-effect spread. "equal" shares across classes; "varying" estimates one per class; "proportional" shares shape lets size differ. random_diagonal = TRUE makes random effects uncorrelated. Curved trajectories. score ~ wave + (wave^2) score ~ splines::ns(wave, df = 3) give curved class trajectories. degenerate covariance. data support random effect class (variance zero, two random effects perfectly correlated), fit warns (latents_random_boundary), reports interval covariance, marks boundary tables plots. random effects simplified removed.

title: Multilevel latent profile analysis with the latents R package
text: n_profiles n_group_classes set numbers profiles group classes; n_starts sets number EM starts, seed makes reproducible cores runs parallel. default covariance structure "VVI" (Celeux & Govaert, 1995): profile-specific variances covariances within profiles, indicators independent given profile. what: Relating the classes to other variables
title: Multilevel latent profile analysis with the latents R package
text: Entering external variable model can change classes meant explain. Three-step methods hold classes fixed correct classification error (Bolck et al., 2004; Vermunt, 2010). r3step() regresses profile membership predictors, last profile, disengaged one, reference. previous grade one standard deviation higher increases log odds engaged enrolment 0.615 (95% interval 0.495 0.735), odds ratio 1.85. three_step() compares mean variable across profiles. Previous grades 0.57 standard deviations lower disengaged engaged enrolments (95% interval 0.47 0.67). results associations; temporal order alone establish effect grades engagement. One-step alternatives enter predictors model (profile_covariates observations, group_covariates groups); fit_staged() holds profiles fixed group classes estimated. covariates case study articles compare approaches.

title: Simulated engagement states and trajectories over a study programme — engagement_momentum
text: engagement_momentum simulated dataset student engagement across courses study programme. row represents one student's enrolment one course, courses ordered within students. every course student one three engagement states (active, average disengaged), measured five activity indicators standardized within course; programme student follows one three trajectories (engaged, fluctuating mostly disengaged). course also grade. design follows study engagement dynamics López-Pernas Saqr (2024): engaged students show momentum, active course tending followed another, mostly disengaged students show inertia, disengaged course tending followed another. parameter values illustrative choices reproduce patterns; estimates study.

code: # Classify new observations with a fitted profile model. profiles <- lpa(faithful, c("eruptions", "waiting"), n_profiles = 2,                 n_starts = 2, seed = 1) predict(profiles, data.frame(eruptions = c(2, 4.5), waiting = c(55, 80)),         type = "posterior") #>   row profile posterior probability_profile_1 probability_profile_2 #> 1   1       2         1          3.110134e-11          1.000000e+00 #> 2   2       1         1          1.000000e+00          1.264747e-23  # The mean outcome under each class of a mixture regression. fit <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,                           n_starts = 2, seed = 1) predict(fit, data.frame(hours = c(2, 10)), type = "class_response") #>   row   class     prior   fitted #> 1   1 class_1 0.5645888 43.49393 #> 2   2 class_1 0.5645888 80.00640 #> 3   1 class_2 0.4354112 56.52305 #> 4   2 class_2 0.4354112 62.96629 head(simulate(fit, nsim = 2, seed = 1)) #>      sim_1    sim_2 #> 1 85.96107 84.66292 #> 2 43.06356 61.01025 #> 3 57.86180 62.03635 #> 4 51.20585 72.29776 #> 5 78.31739 84.47418 #> 6 59.89100 71.01171  # Predict an individual trajectory conditional on observed scores. growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, data = subset(growth_scores, student <= 60),                              n_classes = 2, id = "student", class_level = "group",                              random = ~ 1, n_starts = 1, seed = 1) predict(growth, subset(growth_scores, student == 61), type = "conditional") #>   row   fitted #> 1   1 58.88460 #> 2   2 65.58452 #> 3   3 72.28445 #> 4   4 75.63441

title: Fit a mixture regression model in which the relationship between an outcome and its predictors differs across latent classes — mixture_regression
text: mixture_regression() fits mixture class-specific regressions, relationship outcome predictors differs across latent classes. Classes can differ outcome level, predictor associations trajectory time. Regression parameters class probabilities estimated jointly maximum likelihood. Predictors formula describe variation within classes; covariates membership describe belongs class. coefficient may shared every class (common). Class membership can belong row every row unit (class_level); time predictor shared membership classes trajectories, random adds within-class variation around (growth mixture model). Outcomes can Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative binomial ordinal.

title: Compare latent classes on an outcome not used to define them, correcting for classification error — three_step
code: set.seed(11) group <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 10) truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(400) > 0.5) example_data <- data.frame(   g = group,   a = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),   b = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),   y = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 10, 0)) ) fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,                 n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1) # The mean of `y` in each class, then the difference between the classes. three_step(fit, example_data, "y") #> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI) #>  #> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n #> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  ----------- #>     1  -0.069  [-0.463,  0.325]  0.20       182.74 #>     2   9.972  [ 9.531, 10.412]  0.22       170.37 three_step(fit, example_data, "y", contrast = "pairs") #> Distal outcome: class differences (bch, 95% CI) #>  #> Class  vs  Difference         95% CI      p  p (BH) #> -----  --  ----------  -------------  -----  ------ #>     2   1       10.04  [9.37, 10.72]  <.001   <.001 # A categorical outcome: its probability in each class. example_data <- transform(example_data, passed = y + rnorm(400, sd = 6) > 5) three_step(fit, example_data, "passed") #> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI) #>  #> Class  Category  Probability        95% CI     SE  Effective n #> -----  --------  -----------  ------------  -----  ----------- #>     1  FALSE            0.80  [0.73, 0.85]  0.030       182.74 #>     1  TRUE             0.20  [0.15, 0.27]  0.030       182.74 #>     2  FALSE            0.17  [0.12, 0.23]  0.030       170.37 #>     2  TRUE             0.83  [0.77, 0.88]  0.030       170.37 three_step(fit, example_data, "passed", contrast = "overall") #> Distal outcome: equal across classes (bch, Wald) #>  #>  Wald  df      p #> -----  --  ----- #> 99.11   1  <.001 # An outcome missing for some units: they are left out of step three. example_data <- transform(example_data, y_seen = replace(y, seq_len(25), NA)) three_step(fit, example_data, "y_seen", missing = "exclude") #> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI) #>  #> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n #> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  ----------- #>     1  -0.012  [-0.435,  0.412]  0.22       167.09 #>     2   9.949  [ 9.496, 10.402]  0.23       162.74
